name: Shakuhachi honkyoku
lineage: Japanese Fuke-Zen shakuhachi five-hole bamboo-flute solo tradition with the 36-piece honkyoku canonical-repertoire codified by the Komuso mendicant-monk lineage of the Edo-period (1603-1868). Originated from Tang-dynasty Chinese chi imported via 8th-century Buddhist transmission, transformed through medieval Japanese ascetic-monastic practice into a meditative suizen blowing-as-zen contemplative discipline. Each honkyoku piece is ametrical-rhythmically-free (no fixed pulse), built around the wabi-sabi aesthetic of single-tone meri-kari microtonal bending, atari-and-mura-iki breath-attack and breath-noise as expressive elements, and silence as compositional structure. The Meiji-era 1871 suppression of the Fuke sect transitioned the repertoire from religious to concert context.
